name: scamcheck
description: Analyze a message, a link or a sender for fraud/phishing risk signals with a deterministic heuristic model, and get safety tips and official reporting resources. An analysis of risk signals, not a guaranteed verdict; read-only, stateless, no account.

interface.longDescription: ScamCheck analyzes a message (email, SMS, private message), a single link or domain, or a sender (email address or number) and returns the fraud and phishing risk signals it detects — for example urgency and pressure, a request to pay or to click, a shortened link, a raw IP address, a missing HTTPS, a look-alike or free-address domain. It uses a deterministic heuristic model: the same input always gives the same signals, nothing is generated by a language model, no account is needed, nothing is stored and no file is read. The result is an ANALYSIS of risk signals, not a guaranteed verdict: a high number of signals suggests caution, but the absence of a signal does not prove a message is safe. ScamCheck also returns practical safety tips and official reporting resources (the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre). It is an information and prevention tool; it does not contact anyone, does not report on your behalf and does not open attachments.
capabilities: Analyzes a message, link or sender and flags fraud/phishing risk signals with a deterministic heuristic model.
Returns an analysis of risk signals, not a guaranteed verdict; absence of a signal does not prove a message safe.
Also gives fraud safety tips and official reporting resources. Read-only, stateless, no account, no files read.
defaultPrompt: Is this text a scam? 'Your parcel is on hold, pay a $2 fee at bit.ly/abc to release it.'
Does this sender look legit: support@paypa1-secure.com?
I think I was phished. What should I do?

positive.prompt: Is this text a scam? 'Your parcel is on hold, pay a $2 fee at bit.ly/abc to release it.'
positive.expected_behavior: Calls analyser_message; returns the detected signals (urgency, payment request, shortened link) with a risk level, and states explicitly that this is an analysis of signals, not a guaranteed verdict. Read-only.
Calls analyser_url; flags signals such as a raw IP address and missing HTTPS, returns a risk level, and notes that no signal found would not prove the link safe. Read-only.

positive.prompt: Does this sender look legit: support@paypa1-secure.com ?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls analyser_expediteur; flags look-alike/typosquat and related signals, returns a risk level as an analysis (not a verdict), without asserting the sender is definitely fraudulent. Read-only.

positive.description: Ask what to do after a suspected phishing
positive.prompt: I think I was phished. What should I do?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls conseils_securite; returns practical fraud safety tips and official reporting resources (Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre). It does not report on the user's behalf. Read-only.

positive.prompt: Analyze this message: 'Hi, see you at 3pm for coffee.'
positive.expected_behavior: Calls analyser_message; returns few or no risk signals and a low risk level, but states explicitly that the absence of signals does not prove the message is safe. Read-only.

negative.prompt: What is the capital of France?
negative.expected_behavior: No ScamCheck tool is triggered: this is pure general-knowledge Q&A with nothing to analyze for fraud.

negative.description: Act on the user's behalf (out of scope)
negative.prompt: Report this scammer to the police and block their number for me.
negative.expected_behavior: No ScamCheck tool is triggered: ScamCheck cannot report, contact anyone or block numbers; it can only analyze and give official reporting resources.

negative.prompt: Open the attached PDF and scan it for scams.
negative.expected_behavior: No ScamCheck tool is triggered: ScamCheck does not read or open files; it analyzes a message text, a URL or a sender provided in the conversation.

publication.release_notes: Initial release. ScamCheck analyzes a message, a link or a sender for fraud and phishing risk signals with a deterministic heuristic model, and returns safety tips and official reporting resources (Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre). The four tools (analyser_message, analyser_url, analyser_expediteur, conseils_securite) are read-only and stateless; no account, nothing stored, no files read. The result is an analysis of risk signals, not a guaranteed verdict: the absence of a signal does not prove a message is safe.
